        "contents": "# Minigame Ideas for Abbies World\n\nThis document outlines creative minigame concepts that utilize user-generated images and characters from the app.\n\n---\n\n## 🎮 Implemented Games\n\n### 1. Memory/Concentration Game ✅\n**Status:** Implemented  \n**Location:** &#96;Views/Minigames/MemoryGame/&#96;\n\n**Description:**\n- Classic memory game using user-generated images\n- Players match pairs of their created images\n- Three difficulty levels (Easy: 4 pairs, Medium: 6 pairs, Hard: 8 pairs)\n- Score based on number of moves\n- Beautiful card-flip animations\n\n**Features:**\n- Uses images from user's generation history\n- Automatically creates pairs from available images\n- Tracks moves and score\n- Victory screen with statistics\n\n---\n\n## 💡 Additional Game Ideas\n\n### 2. Character Scene Builder 🎨\n**Type:** Creative/Storytelling  \n**Complexity:** Medium  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nPlayers create scenes using their generated characters and backgrounds. Drag and drop characters into different scenes, add props, and create stories.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Select a background (from user's \"place\" images or generated backgrounds)\n- Drag characters into the scene\n- Position and resize characters\n- Add text bubbles for dialogue\n- Save scenes as new images\n- Share scenes with others\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Use SwiftUI drag-and-drop\n- Canvas-based rendering (similar to WaypointGameCanvas)\n- Image composition to create final scene\n- Save composed images back to server\n\n**Assets Needed:**\n- User's character images (from \"friends\" carousel)\n- Background images (from \"places\" carousel)\n- Optional: Prop/object images\n\n---\n\n### 3. Character Matching Game 🎯\n**Type:** Matching/Puzzle  \n**Complexity:** Low-Medium  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nMatch characters to their outfits, or match characters to the places they belong in. Multiple game modes.\n\n**Game Modes:**\n1. **Outfit Match:** Match character to their outfit\n2. **Place Match:** Match character to their place\n3. **Style Match:** Match character to their art style",

          },
          {
            "text": "**Complexity:** Medium  ",

          },
          {
            "text": "**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "**Description:**",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "Players create scenes using their generated characters and backgrounds. Drag and drop characters into different scenes, add props, and create stories.",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "**Mechanics:**",

          {

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "- Save scenes as new images",

          {

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "- Image composition to create final scene",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "- Save composed images back to server",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },

        "contents": "# Standalone Minigame Pattern\n\n**Based on:** Waypoint Navigation Game  \n**Purpose:** Each minigame should be able to function as a standalone app OR be integrated into the main app\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Pattern\n\n### Key Principle: **Self-Contained Independence**\n\nEach minigame should be completely self-contained and not depend on the main app structure. It should work both:\n1. **Standalone:** As its own app (for testing/debugging)\n2. **Integrated:** As part of the main app (via fullScreenCover/sheet)\n\n---\n\n## File Structure Pattern\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nViews/\n  Minigames/\n    {GameName}/\n      {GameName}View.swift          // Main game view (self-contained)\n      {GameName}Canvas.swift        // SpriteKit/rendering (if needed)\n      {GameName}VictoryView.swift    // Victory sequence (if needed)\nViewModels/\n  {GameName}ViewModel.swift          // Game-specific view model\nModels/\n  {GameName}Models.swift            // Game-specific models\nServices/\n  {GameName}AudioService.swift      // Game-specific audio (if needed)\n{GameName}StandaloneApp.swift       // Standalone entry point\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Component Breakdown\n\n### 1. **Standalone App Entry Point**\n\n**File:** &#96;{GameName}StandaloneApp.swift&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\n//\n//  {GameName}StandaloneApp.swift\n//  abbies.world.ios\n//\n//  Standalone entry point for {Game Name} Minigame\n//  This allows the game to run independently without the main app\n//\n//  NOTE: To run as standalone app:\n//  1. Temporarily comment out @main in abbies_world_iosApp.swift\n//  2. Uncomment @main below\n//  3. Or create a separate Xcode target for the standalone game\n//\n\nimport SwiftUI\n\n// Uncomment the @main attribute below to run as standalone app\n// (and comment out @main in abbies_world_iosApp.swift)\n// @main\nstruct {GameName}StandaloneApp: App {\n    var body: some Scene {\n        WindowGroup {\n            {GameName}View()\n                .ignoresSafeArea()\n        }\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Key Points:**\n- Simple App struct that wraps the main game view\n- &#96;@main&#96; is commented out by default\n- Can be easily enabled for standalone testing",

        "contents": "- Search/filter logic\n\n---\n\n### 9. Character Race Game 🏁\n**Type:** Arcade/Racing  \n**Complexity:** High  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nCharacters race across the screen. Tap to make them jump over obstacles or collect items.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Use character images as racers\n- Side-scrolling or vertical scrolling\n- Tap to jump/action\n- Obstacles and collectibles\n- Power-ups\n- Score based on distance and items collected\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- SpriteKit or SwiftUI animations\n- Physics engine for jumping\n- Obstacle generation\n- Score tracking\n\n---\n\n### 10. Image Guessing Game 🎲\n**Type:** Trivia/Guessing  \n**Complexity:** Low-Medium  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nShow a cropped or modified version of a user's image and guess which one it is from a selection.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Show a cropped/zoomed section of an image\n- Display 4-6 options (one correct, rest random)\n- Multiple rounds\n- Score based on correct guesses\n- Time limit per round\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Image cropping/zooming\n- Random selection of wrong answers\n- Round management\n- Score tracking\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 Recommended Implementation Order\n\n### Phase 1: Quick Wins (High Appeal, Medium Complexity)\n1. ✅ **Memory Game** - DONE\n2. **Character Matching Game** - Reuses existing image loading, simple drag-and-drop\n3. **Image Puzzle Game** - Classic mechanic, straightforward implementation\n\n### Phase 2: Creative Games (High Appeal, Medium-High Complexity)\n4. **Character Scene Builder** - Most creative, high engagement\n5. **Image Story Sequence** - Builds on scene builder concepts\n6. **Character Dress-Up Game** - Fun customization\n\n### Phase 3: Additional Features\n7. **Character Hide &amp; Seek** - Good variety\n8. **Character Collection Album** - Organizational tool\n9. **Character Race Game** - More complex, requires physics\n10. **Image Guessing Game** - Simple but engaging\n\n---\n\n## 🛠️ Technical Considerations\n\n### Shared Components\n- **Image Loading:** Use existing &#96;ImageCache.shared&#96; and &#96;APIClient.shared&#96;\n- **Game Pattern:** Follow &#96;STANDALONE_MINIGAME_PATTERN.md&#96; for consistency",

        "contents": "# Phaser Minigames Porting Plan for Swift iOS\n\n**Date:** December 2025  \n**Source:** &#96;/Users/evanrobinson/abbies_world_2023/abbiesworld&#96;  \n**Target:** Swift iOS App (abbies.world.ios)\n\n---\n\n## Executive Summary\n\n**Total Games Available:** 15  \n**Functional Games:** 10  \n**Non-Functional (Need Fixes):** 5  \n**Recommended Porting Order:** Based on complexity and kid appeal\n\n**Current Status:** Waypoint Navigation game is complete. Ready to port additional minigames.\n\n---\n\n## Game Inventory &amp; Status\n\n### ✅ **Fully Functional Games (Ready to Port)**\n\n#### 1. **FindJungle** ✅\n- **Type:** Hidden Object Finder\n- **Complexity:** Medium\n- **Assets:**\n  - 4-5 backgrounds (&#96;background1.png&#96; - &#96;background5.png&#96;)\n  - 170+ object sprites (&#96;0.png&#96; - &#96;169.png&#96;)\n  - UI elements (&#96;ui1.png&#96; - &#96;ui5.png&#96;, &#96;foundImage.png&#96;, &#96;playButton.png&#96;)\n  - Magnifier tool (&#96;magnifier.png&#96;)\n- **Mechanics:**\n  - Timer-based gameplay\n  - Random object selection (5 objects to find from 25 available)\n  - Hint system with magnifier\n  - Score tracking\n  - Multiple backgrounds\n- **Swift Port Complexity:** Medium\n- **Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (High - visual search is engaging)\n\n#### 2. **FindPirates** ✅\n- **Type:** Hidden Object Finder\n- **Complexity:** Medium\n- **Assets:** Similar structure to FindJungle\n- **Mechanics:** Same as FindJungle\n- **Swift Port Complexity:** Medium\n- **Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (High - pirate theme)\n\n#### 3. **FindCarnival** ✅\n- **Type:** Hidden Object Finder\n- **Complexity:** Medium\n- **Assets:** 5 backgrounds + objects\n- **Mechanics:** Same pattern as other Find games\n- **Swift Port Complexity:** Medium\n- **Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Very High - carnival theme)\n\n#### 4. **FindPrincess** ✅\n- **Type:** Hidden Object Finder\n- **Complexity:** Medium\n- **Assets:** 20 objects to find\n- **Mechanics:** Same pattern\n- **Swift Port Complexity:** Medium\n- **Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (Very High - princess theme)\n\n#### 5. **FindFarm** ✅\n- **Type:** Hidden Object Finder\n- **Complexity:** Medium\n- **Assets:** Similar structure",

        "contents": "2. **Place Match:** Match character to their place\n3. **Style Match:** Match character to their art style\n4. **Mixed Match:** Random combinations\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Grid of characters on one side\n- Grid of outfits/places/styles on the other\n- Drag and drop to match\n- Feedback animations (correct = green check, wrong = red X)\n- Timer mode for added challenge\n- Score based on accuracy and speed\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Use recipeItems from GeneratedImage to determine correct matches\n- Drag-and-drop interface\n- Match validation logic\n- Score calculation\n\n---\n\n### 4. Image Story Sequence 📖\n**Type:** Storytelling/Creative  \n**Complexity:** Medium  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nArrange user-generated images in sequence to tell a story. Create comic strips or storyboards.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Select 3-6 images from user's history\n- Arrange them in order\n- Add text captions to each image\n- Choose transitions between images\n- Play back as an animated story\n- Export as video or image sequence\n\n**Features:**\n- Drag to reorder images\n- Text overlay editor\n- Transition effects (fade, slide, zoom)\n- Story playback mode\n- Save stories to share\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Image sequence management\n- Text overlay rendering\n- Animation/transition system\n- Video export (using AVFoundation)\n\n---\n\n### 5. Character Hide &amp; Seek 🔍\n**Type:** Hidden Object  \n**Complexity:** Medium  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nFind hidden characters in a scene. Characters are partially hidden or disguised in the background.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Use a generated image as the scene\n- Hide character images within the scene (blended, scaled, rotated)\n- Player clicks/taps to find characters\n- Timer-based gameplay\n- Hint system (highlight area after X seconds)\n- Score based on time and hints used\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Image compositing to hide characters\n- Touch detection for finding characters\n- Timer system\n- Hint system with visual feedback\n\n---\n\n### 6. Character Dress-Up Game 👗\n**Type:** Creative/Customization  ",

        "contents": "# Voice Integration Opportunities for Abbies World iOS App\n\n## Overview\nThis document outlines approximately 20 different places where voice narration, guidance, or audio feedback could enhance the user experience in the app. These suggestions are organized by app section and user flow.\n\n---\n\n## 1. **App Onboarding &amp; First Launch**\n\n### 1.1 Welcome Message\n**Location:** &#96;MainView.onAppear&#96; / &#96;MainViewModel.loadData()&#96;\n**Voice:** \"Welcome to Abbies World! Swipe through the carousels to choose a friend, outfit, and place. When you're ready, tap the generate button to create your image.\"\n**Purpose:** First-time user guidance\n\n### 1.2 Feature Discovery\n**Location:** After first successful image generation\n**Voice:** \"Great job! You can swipe from the right edge to see your creation history, or tap the settings icon to customize your experience.\"\n**Purpose:** Teach users about drawer and settings\n\n---\n\n## 2. **Main View - Carousel Interactions**\n\n### 2.3 Carousel Selection Feedback\n**Location:** &#96;CarouselView.onSelect&#96; / &#96;MainViewModel.selectFriend/Outfit/Place&#96;\n**Voice:** When user selects an item, announce: \"You selected [Friend Name]\" or \"Outfit chosen: [Outfit Name]\"\n**Purpose:** Audio confirmation of selections, especially helpful for accessibility\n\n### 2.4 Selection Progress Updates\n**Location:** &#96;MainViewModel.updateButtonState()&#96; when selections change\n**Voice:** \n- After 1 selection: \"One more selection needed\"\n- After 2 selections: \"Almost there! Just need one more\"\n- After 3 selections: \"All set! Ready to generate\"\n**Purpose:** Guide users toward completion\n\n### 2.5 Style Carousel Guidance (4-Carousel Mode)\n**Location:** &#96;FourCarouselView&#96; when styleIndex is -1\n**Voice:** \"Don't forget to choose an art style! This will change how your image looks.\"\n**Purpose:** Remind users about the 4th carousel option\n\n---\n\n## 3. **Image Generation Flow**\n\n### 3.6 Generation Start Confirmation\n**Location:** &#96;MainViewModel.startImageGeneration()&#96; when generation begins\n**Voice:** \"Creating your image now! This might take a moment...\"\n**Purpose:** Confirm action and set expectations",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "# Voice Integration Opportunities for Abbies World iOS App\n\n## Overview\nThis document outlines approximately 20 different places where voice narration, guidance, or audio feedback could enhance the user experience in the app. These suggestions are organized by app section and user flow.\n\n---\n\n## 1. **App Onboarding &amp; First Launch**\n\n### 1.1 Welcome Message\n**Location:** &#96;MainView.onAppear&#96; / &#96;MainViewModel.loadData()&#96;\n**Voice:** \"Welcome to Abbies World! Swipe through the carousels to choose a friend, outfit, and place. When you're ready, tap the generate button to create your image.\"\n**Purpose:** First-time user guidance\n\n### 1.2 Feature Discovery\n**Location:** After first successful image generation\n**Voice:** \"Great job! You can swipe from the right edge to see your creation history, or tap the settings icon to customize your experience.\"\n**Purpose:** Teach users about drawer and settings\n\n---\n\n## 2. **Main View - Carousel Interactions**\n\n### 2.3 Carousel Selection Feedback\n**Location:** &#96;CarouselView.onSelect&#96; / &#96;MainViewModel.selectFriend/Outfit/Place&#96;\n**Voice:** When user selects an item, announce: \"You selected [Friend Name]\" or \"Outfit chosen: [Outfit Name]\"\n**Purpose:** Audio confirmation of selections, especially helpful for accessibility\n\n### 2.4 Selection Progress Updates\n**Location:** &#96;MainViewModel.updateButtonState()&#96; when selections change\n**Voice:** \n- After 1 selection: \"One more selection needed\"\n- After 2 selections: \"Almost there! Just need one more\"\n- After 3 selections: \"All set! Ready to generate\"\n**Purpose:** Guide users toward completion\n\n### 2.5 Style Carousel Guidance (4-Carousel Mode)\n**Location:** &#96;FourCarouselView&#96; when styleIndex is -1\n**Voice:** \"Don't forget to choose an art style! This will change how your image looks.\"\n**Purpose:** Remind users about the 4th carousel option\n\n---\n\n## 3. **Image Generation Flow**\n\n### 3.6 Generation Start Confirmation\n**Location:** &#96;MainViewModel.startImageGeneration()&#96; when generation begins\n**Voice:** \"Creating your image now! This might take a moment...\"\n**Purpose:** Confirm action and set expectations",

        "contents": "# Music Playback Implementation - Complete\n\n## ✅ What Was Built\n\n### 1. **MusicTrack Model** (&#96;Models/MusicTrack.swift&#96;)\n- Represents a single music track with metadata\n- Converts from &#96;Asset&#96; model\n- Provides cleaned display names (removes .mp3, replaces underscores)\n- Includes &#96;RepeatMode&#96; enum (all, one, none)\n\n### 2. **MusicService** (&#96;Services/MusicService.swift&#96;)\n**Core Features:**\n- ✅ Fetches music playlist from server via AssetsService\n- ✅ Caches playlist to UserDefaults (24-hour validity)\n- ✅ Caches audio files to disk (&#96;Documents/MusicCache/&#96;)\n- ✅ Playback management with AVAudioPlayer\n- ✅ Shuffle mode (generates random queue)\n- ✅ Repeat mode (all, one, none)\n- ✅ Song selection (play specific song, then continue queue)\n- ✅ Game coordination (pauses when game starts, resumes when game ends)\n- ✅ Audio interruption handling (phone calls, etc.)\n- ✅ Settings persistence (shuffle, music on/off, current song)\n- ✅ Auto-play on startup if music enabled\n\n**Key Methods:**\n- &#96;loadPlaylist()&#96; - Fetch from server, cache locally\n- &#96;play()&#96; / &#96;pause()&#96; / &#96;stop()&#96; - Playback control\n- &#96;toggleMusic()&#96; - Enable/disable music\n- &#96;toggleShuffle()&#96; - Enable/disable shuffle\n- &#96;playSong(_:)&#96; - Play specific song\n- &#96;setGameActive(_:)&#96; - Coordinate with game lifecycle\n\n### 3. **SettingsView Updates** (&#96;Views/Components/SettingsView.swift&#96;)\n**New Music Controls Section:**\n- ✅ Music On/Off toggle\n- ✅ Shuffle On/Off toggle\n- ✅ Song selector list with:\n  - Currently playing indicator (▶️ icon)\n  - Play/pause state display\n  - Tap to select and play song\n  - Highlighted current song\n\n### 4. **MainView Integration**\n- ✅ Game lifecycle coordination via &#96;.onChange(of: showWaypointGame)&#96;\n- ✅ Calls &#96;MusicService.shared.setGameActive()&#96; when game starts/ends\n\n### 5. **MainViewModel Integration**\n- ✅ Initializes &#96;MusicService.shared&#96; on app startup\n- ✅ Music service loads playlist automatically\n\n## 🎯 How It Works\n\n### Startup Flow:\n1. App launches → &#96;MainViewModel.init()&#96; → &#96;MusicService.shared&#96; created\n2. &#96;MusicService.init()&#96; → Checks cache → Loads playlist (cache or server)",

        "contents": "### 6. Character Dress-Up Game 👗\n**Type:** Creative/Customization  \n**Complexity:** Low-Medium  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nDress up characters with different outfits. Mix and match to create new looks.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Select a base character\n- Choose from available outfits (from user's generated images)\n- Layer outfits on character\n- Save new combinations\n- Create \"fashion show\" with multiple looks\n\n**Features:**\n- Drag-and-drop outfit selection\n- Layer management (which outfit goes on top)\n- Preview mode\n- Save favorite combinations\n- Share looks\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Image layering/compositing\n- Outfit detection and extraction from generated images\n- Layer management system\n\n---\n\n### 7. Image Puzzle Game 🧩\n**Type:** Puzzle  \n**Complexity:** Low-Medium  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nClassic jigsaw puzzle using user-generated images. Break images into pieces and reassemble.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- Select an image from user's history\n- Break into puzzle pieces (4x4, 6x6, 8x8 grid)\n- Drag pieces to correct positions\n- Timer and move counter\n- Hint system (show outline)\n- Difficulty levels (piece count)\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Image slicing algorithm\n- Grid-based puzzle system\n- Drag-and-drop for pieces\n- Position validation\n- Puzzle state management\n\n---\n\n### 8. Character Collection Album 📸\n**Type:** Collection/Organization  \n**Complexity:** Low  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐\n\n**Description:**\nOrganize and categorize user-generated images. Create albums, add tags, and browse collections.\n\n**Mechanics:**\n- View all generated images in a grid\n- Create custom albums/categories\n- Drag images into albums\n- Add tags/labels to images\n- Search and filter\n- Share albums\n\n**Features:**\n- Visual album organization\n- Tag system\n- Search functionality\n- Export albums as PDF or image grid\n\n**Technical Implementation:**\n- Image grid view\n- Album data structure\n- Tag management\n- Search/filter logic\n\n---\n\n### 9. Character Race Game 🏁\n**Type:** Arcade/Racing  \n**Complexity:** High  \n**Kid Appeal:** ⭐⭐⭐⭐",

        "contents": "# Project Review: Abbie's World iOS - Waypoint Navigation Game\n\n**Date:** December 2025  \n**Project Type:** Swift iOS Game for Kids  \n**Reviewer:** AI Code Assistant\n\n---\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nThis is a **well-architected Swift game** built for a child, featuring a waypoint navigation puzzle game with a multi-phase victory sequence. The codebase demonstrates good Swift/SwiftUI practices, proper separation of concerns, and thoughtful error handling.\n\n**Overall Assessment:** ✅ **Good** - Production-ready with some security and polish improvements recommended\n\n**Key Strengths:**\n- Clean MVVM architecture\n- Comprehensive error handling\n- Good use of modern Swift patterns (async/await, Combine)\n- Thoughtful asset loading and caching\n- Complete game mechanics implementation\n\n**Key Concerns:**\n- 🔴 **Security:** API key stored in Info.plist (visible in app bundle)\n- 🟡 **Performance:** Image processing on main thread\n- 🟡 **UX:** Some minor polish items for better kid experience\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Review\n\n### ✅ **Excellent Structure**\n\nThe project follows a clean MVVM pattern with clear separation:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nViews/\n  ├── MainView.swift (main app)\n  ├── WaypointNavigationGame/\n  │   ├── WaypointNavigationView.swift\n  │   ├── WaypointGameCanvas.swift (SpriteKit)\n  │   └── VictorySequenceView.swift\nViewModels/\n  ├── MainViewModel.swift\n  └── WaypointGameViewModel.swift\nModels/\n  └── WaypointGameModels.swift\nServices/\n  ├── APIClient.swift\n  ├── ServerConfig.swift\n  ├── ImageCache.swift\n  ├── AssetsService.swift\n  └── WaypointGameAudioService.swift\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Strengths:**\n- Clear separation of concerns\n- Services are well-organized\n- ViewModels properly manage state\n- Models are simple and focused\n\n### Code Quality\n\n**Swift Best Practices:**\n- ✅ Proper use of &#96;@Published&#96; and &#96;ObservableObject&#96;\n- ✅ Weak references in closures (&#96;[weak self]&#96;)\n- ✅ Proper async/await usage\n- ✅ Good error handling with descriptive messages\n- ✅ Comprehensive logging with emoji prefixes for readability",

        "contents": "**Priority Order:**\n1. **goonpopper** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐\n   - Simple mechanics\n   - High kid appeal\n   - Good for testing porting patterns\n   - **Estimated Time:** 4-6 hours\n\n2. **FindPrincess** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐\n   - High kid appeal\n   - Reusable pattern for other Find games\n   - **Estimated Time:** 6-8 hours\n\n3. **FindCarnival** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐\n   - High kid appeal\n   - Can reuse FindPrincess pattern\n   - **Estimated Time:** 4-6 hours (after FindPrincess)\n\n### Phase 2: Medium Complexity Games\n\n4. **FindJungle** ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n   - More objects than FindPrincess\n   - Reuses FindPrincess pattern\n   - **Estimated Time:** 4-6 hours\n\n5. **FindFarm** ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n   - Same pattern\n   - **Estimated Time:** 4-6 hours\n\n6. **FindPirates** ⭐⭐⭐⭐\n   - Same pattern\n   - **Estimated Time:** 4-6 hours\n\n7. **puzzle** ⭐⭐⭐⭐ (after fixing)\n   - Different mechanics (drag-and-drop)\n   - Good variety\n   - **Estimated Time:** 6-8 hours\n\n### Phase 3: Complex Games\n\n8. **Tracer3** ⭐⭐⭐\n   - Complex geometry calculations\n   - Multiple levels\n   - Audio integration\n   - **Estimated Time:** 12-16 hours\n\n9. **enchantedforest** ⭐⭐⭐\n   - World navigation\n   - Camera system\n   - **Estimated Time:** 8-10 hours\n\n10. **FindSpace** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (after fixing)\n    - Fix Phaser version first\n    - Then port\n    - **Estimated Time:** 4-6 hours\n\n### Phase 4: Lower Priority\n\n11. **bubblepopper** (after fixing)\n12. **Tracer2** (after fixing)\n13. **MyTracerGame** (after fixing)\n14. **clippingMask** (demo only)\n15. **scripts/main.js** (main world map - may integrate differently)\n\n---\n\n## Swift Porting Architecture Recommendations\n\n### ⚠️ **CRITICAL: Standalone App Pattern**\n\n**Each minigame MUST follow the standalone app pattern** (see &#96;STANDALONE_MINIGAME_PATTERN.md&#96; for details).\n\n**Key Requirements:**\n- ✅ Self-contained view with &#96;@StateObject&#96; ViewModel\n- ✅ Optional callbacks (&#96;onDismiss&#96;, &#96;onComplete&#96;) for integration\n- ✅ Works perfectly without callbacks (standalone mode)\n- ✅ Own asset loading and state management\n- ✅ Standalone app entry point file (&#96;{GameName}StandaloneApp.swift&#96;)",

        "contents": "# Prompt Customization Feature - Ideation Document\n\n**Date:** December 2025  \n**Feature:** Enhanced Prompt Customization for Image Generation  \n**Target Audience:** Children (with varying reading/writing abilities)\n\n---\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nCurrently, reference images (friend, outfit, place) are forcing generated outputs to always include borders, limiting visual variety. Users need more control over how images are generated without losing the simplicity that makes the app accessible to children.\n\n---\n\n## Current Architecture\n\n### API Request Structure (&#96;CreateRequest&#96;)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nstruct CreateRequest {\n    let recipeItems: [RecipeItem]           // Selected ingredient IDs\n    let freeTextDescription: String?        // Currently used for style descriptions\n    let referenceImageIds: [String]?        // Reference images (friend, outfit, place)\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Current Flow\n1. User selects friend, outfit, place (and optionally style in 4-carousel mode)\n2. Reference images are extracted and sent to server\n3. Style (if selected) is passed as text in &#96;freeTextDescription&#96;\n4. Server generates image using reference images + text description\n\n### The Issue\n- Reference images contain borders → AI model copies borders to output\n- No way to control border presence\n- Limited variety in output styles\n\n---\n\n## Solution Concepts (Child-Friendly)\n\n### Concept 1: Visual Toggle Controls (Simplest - Ages 4-7)\n\n**Idea:** Simple on/off toggles with icons and minimal text\n\n**Controls:**\n- 🖼️ **Border Toggle** - \"Picture Frame\" (on/off)\n  - Icon: Frame/border icon\n  - Label: \"Add Frame\" or \"No Frame\"\n  - Default: On (matches current behavior)\n\n- 🎨 **Color Intensity** - \"More Colorful\" slider\n  - Visual slider with emoji indicators\n  - Low: 🎨 (normal)\n  - High: 🌈 (very colorful)\n  - Default: Middle\n\n- ✨ **Detail Level** - \"More Details\" slider\n  - Low: Simple shapes\n  - High: Lots of details\n  - Default: Middle\n\n**UI Location:** Settings panel → New \"Image Style\" section\n\n**Implementation:**\n- Store preferences in &#96;UserDefaults&#96;",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "### Startup Flow:\n1. App launches → &#96;MainViewModel.init()&#96; → &#96;MusicService.shared&#96; created\n2. &#96;MusicService.init()&#96; → Checks cache → Loads playlist (cache or server)\n3. If music enabled → Auto-plays first song\n\n### Playback Flow:\n1. Song ends → &#96;audioPlayerDidFinishPlaying&#96; delegate called\n2. Check repeat mode:\n   - &#96;.one&#96; → Already looping, continue\n   - &#96;.all&#96; → Move to next song (respects shuffle)\n   - &#96;.none&#96; → Stop playback\n3. Load next song → Cache check → Play\n\n### Game Coordination:\n1. User opens game → &#96;showWaypointGame = true&#96;\n2. &#96;MainView.onChange&#96; → &#96;MusicService.setGameActive(true)&#96;\n3. Music pauses, remembers state\n4. Game ends → &#96;showWaypointGame = false&#96;\n5. &#96;MusicService.setGameActive(false)&#96; → Resumes if was playing\n\n### Interruption Handling:\n1. Phone call / other app → &#96;AVAudioSession.interruptionNotification&#96;\n2. Music pauses, remembers state\n3. Interruption ends → Resumes if appropriate\n\n## 📁 Files Created/Modified\n\n**New Files:**\n- &#96;Models/MusicTrack.swift&#96;\n- &#96;Services/MusicService.swift&#96;\n\n**Modified Files:**\n- &#96;Views/Components/SettingsView.swift&#96; - Added music controls\n- &#96;Views/MainView.swift&#96; - Added game coordination\n- &#96;ViewModels/MainViewModel.swift&#96; - Initialize music service\n\n## 🧪 Testing Checklist\n\n- [ ] Music loads on app startup\n- [ ] Playlist appears in Settings\n- [ ] Music toggle works\n- [ ] Shuffle toggle works\n- [ ] Song selection works\n- [ ] Music pauses when game starts\n- [ ] Music resumes when game ends\n- [ ] Music handles phone calls (interruptions)\n- [ ] Settings persist across app restarts\n- [ ] Cache works offline\n- [ ] Playback continues through playlist\n- [ ] Repeat mode works\n\n## 🐛 Known Issues / Future Improvements\n\n- Repeat mode selector UI (currently defaults to &#96;.all&#96;)\n- Volume control slider\n- Now playing info in drawer\n- Fade in/out between songs\n- Playback progress indicator\n\n## 🎉 Ready to Test!\n\nThe music system is fully implemented and ready for testing. All core features are in place:\n- ✅ Playlist loading with caching\n- ✅ Playback with shuffle/repeat",

        "contents": "   - **Fix:** Move to background queue\n\n2. **Waypoint Click Detection**\n   - O(n) search through all waypoints\n   - Fine for 19 waypoints, but could optimize\n   - **Fix:** Use spatial indexing if adding more waypoints\n\n3. **Timer Usage**\n   - Multiple timers running simultaneously\n   - Properly cleaned up in &#96;deinit&#96;\n   - ✅ Good: Uses weak references\n\n---\n\n## User Experience (Kid-Friendly)\n\n### ✅ **Excellent UX Features**\n\n1. **Clear Visual Feedback**\n   - Color-coded waypoints (cyan → green/red)\n   - Status messages with emojis\n   - Path visualization\n\n2. **Forgiving Gameplay**\n   - Can click unsafe waypoints anytime (no penalty)\n   - Clear error messages for wrong order\n   - Screen shake provides tactile feedback\n\n3. **Engaging Victory Sequence**\n   - Multi-phase celebration\n   - Polaroid carousel (interactive)\n   - Visual rewards for completion\n\n### 🟡 **UX Improvements for Kids**\n\n1. **Instructions Clarity**\n   - Current: \"Discover the safe waypoints to chart the path home!\"\n   - Could be: \"Find the safe path by clicking the waypoints in order!\"\n   - More direct for younger players\n\n2. **Error Messages**\n   - Current: \"⚠️ You must find the waypoints in order!\"\n   - Good, but could add: \"Try clicking a different waypoint!\"\n\n3. **Visual Hints**\n   - Consider highlighting the next safe waypoint after a delay\n   - Or add a \"Hint\" button (optional)\n\n4. **Accessibility**\n   - Consider larger touch targets for younger kids\n   - Add haptic feedback (already has screen shake)\n   - Voice-over support for instructions\n\n---\n\n## Code-Specific Issues\n\n### 1. **Status Message Logic**\n\n**Location:** &#96;WaypointGameViewModel.swift:443-449&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nprivate func updateStatusMessage() {\n    if gameState.clickedGoodNodes == 0 {\n        gameState.statusMessage = \"Click any waypoint to begin discovering the safe path!\"\n    } else {\n        gameState.statusMessage = \"Find the first safe waypoint! (0/\\(gameState.totalGoodNodes))\"\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Issue:** The &#96;else&#96; branch always shows \"0\" even when &#96;clickedGoodNodes &gt; 0&#96;.\n\n**Fix:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\ngameState.statusMessage = \"Find the first safe waypoint! (\\(gameState.clickedGoodNodes)/\\(gameState.totalGoodNodes))\"",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "   - **Fix:** Move to background queue",
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **Waypoint Click Detection**",

          },

            "text": "   - Fine for 19 waypoints, but could optimize",

          {
            "text": "   - **Fix:** Use spatial indexing if adding more waypoints",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "3. **Timer Usage**",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - Multiple timers running simultaneously",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - Properly cleaned up in &#96;deinit&#96;",

          },
          {

        "contents": "# Audio Coordination Pattern\n\n**Status:** ✅ **IMPLEMENTED** - Pattern established and working\n\n## Overview\n\nThe app uses **independent audio services with lifecycle coordination** rather than a centralized audio manager. This approach keeps services decoupled while ensuring they don't conflict.\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Services\n\n1. **MusicService** (Main App)\n   - Singleton: &#96;MusicService.shared&#96;\n   - Manages background music playlist\n   - Pauses when games start, resumes when games end\n\n2. **Game Audio Services** (Minigames)\n   - Each minigame has its own audio service\n   - Examples: &#96;WaypointGameAudioService&#96;, &#96;GoonPopperAudioService&#96;\n   - All inherit from &#96;BaseGameAudioService&#96; for consistency\n   - Stop automatically when game view is dismissed\n\n### Coordination Flow\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser opens minigame\n  ↓\nMainView.onChange detects game state change\n  ↓\nMusicService.setGameActive(true) called\n  ↓\nMusicService pauses background music (remembers state)\n  ↓\nGame audio service starts playing\n  ↓\n[Game plays with its own audio]\n  ↓\nUser closes minigame\n  ↓\nGame audio service stops (in deinit)\n  ↓\nMainView.onChange detects game closed\n  ↓\nMusicService.setGameActive(false) called\n  ↓\nMusicService resumes background music (if it was playing)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Implementation Details\n\n### MusicService Coordination\n\n**Location:** &#96;Services/MusicService.swift&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nfunc setGameActive(_ active: Bool) {\n    if active {\n        wasPlayingBeforeGame = isPlaying\n        if isPlaying {\n            pause()\n        }\n    } else {\n        if wasPlayingBeforeGame &amp;&amp; isMusicEnabled {\n            play()\n        }\n        wasPlayingBeforeGame = false\n    }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Key Features:**\n- Remembers if music was playing before game started\n- Pauses music when game becomes active\n- Resumes music when game ends (only if it was playing before)\n\n### BaseGameAudioService\n\n**Location:** &#96;Services/BaseGameAudioService.swift&#96;\n\nProvides common functionality for all minigame audio services:\n\n- Consistent audio session setup\n- Standard background music loading",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "- &#96;WaypointGameStandaloneApp.swift&#96; ✅\n- &#96;Views/WaypointNavigationGame/WaypointNavigationView.swift&#96; ✅\n- &#96;ViewModels/WaypointGameViewModel.swift&#96; ✅\n- &#96;Models/WaypointGameModels.swift&#96; ✅\n- &#96;Services/WaypointGameAudioService.swift&#96; ✅\n\n### Standalone Usage:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\n// Uncomment @main in WaypointGameStandaloneApp.swift\n// Comment @main in abbies_world_iosApp.swift\n// Run → Game launches directly\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Integrated Usage:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\n// In MainView.swift\n.fullScreenCover(isPresented: $showWaypointGame) {\n    WaypointNavigationView(\n        onDismiss: { showWaypointGame = false },\n        onComplete: { showWaypointGame = false }\n    )\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Checklist for New Minigame\n\nWhen creating a new minigame, ensure:\n\n- [ ] **Standalone App File**\n  - [ ] &#96;{GameName}StandaloneApp.swift&#96; created\n  - [ ] &#96;@main&#96; commented out by default\n  - [ ] Wraps main game view\n\n- [ ] **Main Game View**\n  - [ ] Uses &#96;@StateObject&#96; for ViewModel\n  - [ ] Optional &#96;onDismiss&#96; and &#96;onComplete&#96; callbacks\n  - [ ] Works without callbacks\n  - [ ] Manages own lifecycle\n\n- [ ] **Game ViewModel**\n  - [ ] Self-contained state management\n  - [ ] Uses &#96;ServerConfig.shared&#96; for URLs\n  - [ ] Own asset loading\n  - [ ] Proper cleanup methods\n\n- [ ] **Game Models**\n  - [ ] All game types in one file\n  - [ ] &#96;ObservableObject&#96; for state\n  - [ ] Default configurations\n\n- [ ] **Audio Service** (if needed)\n  - [ ] Self-contained audio management\n  - [ ] Proper cleanup\n\n- [ ] **Asset Organization**\n  - [ ] Assets organized on server\n  - [ ] Uses &#96;ImageCache.shared&#96;\n  - [ ] Graceful error handling\n\n- [ ] **Integration**\n  - [ ] Can be added to MainView via &#96;fullScreenCover&#96;/&#96;sheet&#96;\n  - [ ] Optional callbacks work\n  - [ ] Works standalone\n\n---\n\n## Benefits of This Pattern\n\n1. **Testability:** Each game can be tested independently\n2. **Modularity:** Games don't depend on each other\n3. **Reusability:** Games can be extracted to separate apps\n4. **Maintainability:** Clear boundaries between games\n5. **Debugging:** Easy to isolate issues to specific games\n6. **Flexibility:** Can add/remove games without affecting others\n\n---",

        "contents": "| FindSpace | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | Medium | 4-6h | Medium* |\n| enchantedforest | ⭐⭐⭐ | Medium | 8-10h | Low |\n| Tracer3 | ⭐⭐⭐ | High | 12-16h | Low |\n\n*After fixing Phaser version\n\n---\n\n## Next Steps\n\n### Immediate Actions:\n\n1. **Choose First Game to Port**\n   - Recommended: **goonpopper** (simplest, high appeal)\n   - Or: **FindPrincess** (establishes Find game pattern)\n\n2. **Set Up Asset Structure**\n   - Create server directories\n   - Upload assets for chosen game\n   - Test asset loading\n\n3. **Create Base Components**\n   - &#96;BaseMinigameViewModel&#96;\n   - &#96;MinigameAssetService&#96;\n   - Shared timer/score components\n\n4. **Port First Game**\n   - Follow Waypoint game pattern\n   - Use SpriteKit for rendering\n   - Implement game mechanics\n   - Test on device\n\n### Long-term:\n\n5. **Port Remaining Games** (following priority order)\n6. **Fix Broken Games** (if needed)\n7. **Create Game Selection UI** (carousel/menu)\n8. **Add Progress Tracking** (scores, completion)\n9. **Add Achievements** (optional)\n\n---\n\n## Questions to Consider\n\n1. **Game Selection UI:** How should kids navigate between games?\n   - Carousel (like current ingredient selection)?\n   - Grid view?\n   - World map (like enchantedforest)?\n\n2. **Progress Tracking:** Should games track:\n   - High scores?\n   - Completion status?\n   - Time records?\n\n3. **Unlocking System:** Should games unlock progressively?\n   - Or all available from start?\n\n4. **Audio:** For games with voice lines (Tracer3):\n   - Include all audio?\n   - Or simplify for iOS?\n\n---\n\n**Ready to start porting!** Recommend beginning with **goonpopper** or **FindPrincess** to establish patterns for the rest.",

          {
            "text": "1. **Game Selection UI:** How should kids navigate between games?",

          },
          {

        "contents": "- **Image Loading:** Use existing &#96;ImageCache.shared&#96; and &#96;APIClient.shared&#96;\n- **Game Pattern:** Follow &#96;STANDALONE_MINIGAME_PATTERN.md&#96; for consistency\n- **State Management:** Use &#96;@StateObject&#96; ViewModels with &#96;ObservableObject&#96;\n- **Asset Management:** Load from server using existing asset infrastructure\n\n### New Components Needed\n- **Drag-and-Drop System:** SwiftUI drag-and-drop for matching/scene building\n- **Image Compositing:** Core Image or UIKit for layering images\n- **Animation System:** SwiftUI animations or SpriteKit for complex games\n- **Video Export:** AVFoundation for story sequence export\n\n### Server Integration\n- **Save Game States:** Optional - save high scores, favorite scenes\n- **Share Features:** Export images/videos to share\n- **Leaderboards:** Optional - compare scores with others\n\n---\n\n## 📝 Notes\n\n- All games should follow the standalone minigame pattern\n- Games should gracefully handle cases where users have few/no images\n- Consider adding tutorial/help screens for each game\n- Add sound effects and music where appropriate\n- Ensure games work well on different screen sizes (iPad/iPhone)\n- Consider accessibility features (voice-over, larger touch targets)\n\n---\n\n## 🎨 Design Principles\n\n1. **Use User Content:** All games should prominently feature user-generated images\n2. **Simple Controls:** Touch-friendly, intuitive interactions\n3. **Visual Feedback:** Clear animations and visual cues\n4. **Progressive Difficulty:** Start easy, increase challenge\n5. **Celebrate Success:** Victory screens, achievements, rewards\n6. **Replayability:** Multiple difficulty levels, random generation\n\n---\n\n**Last Updated:** December 2025  \n**Status:** Memory Game implemented, other games are concepts ready for implementation",

        "contents": "**Code Changes:**\n- Add &#96;LoadingView&#96; component with progress bar\n- Track loading progress: &#96;(loadedImages / totalImages) * 100&#96;\n- Pre-load visible carousel tiles before showing UI\n\n**Benefits:**\n- Professional feel\n- Smooth first interaction\n- Clear feedback to user\n\n### Option 2: Keep Current + Add Progress Indicator\n\n**Implementation:**\n1. Keep lazy loading\n2. Add subtle progress indicator (top of screen)\n3. Show \"Loading assets...\" while initial batch loads\n4. Hide when first screen of tiles are ready\n\n**Code Changes:**\n- Minimal - just add progress indicator to &#96;MainView&#96;\n- Track: &#96;(loadedImages / visibleImages) * 100&#96;\n\n**Benefits:**\n- Less code changes\n- Still fast initial render\n- Better feedback\n\n### Option 3: Background Pre-fetching (Advanced)\n\n**Implementation:**\n1. Load metadata on startup (current)\n2. Show UI immediately (current)\n3. Pre-fetch all images in background with low priority\n4. Images appear as they're ready\n\n**Code Changes:**\n- Add background task to pre-fetch all asset images\n- Use &#96;URLSessionConfiguration.background&#96;\n- Prioritize visible tiles, then background\n\n**Benefits:**\n- Best user experience\n- Smooth scrolling\n- Complex to implement\n\n---\n\n## What Most Apps Do\n\n**For apps with 100+ images:**\n\n1. **Games/Media Apps:** Pre-load with loading screen (Pattern 1)\n   - User expects loading time\n   - Better to wait than see spinners everywhere\n\n2. **Social/Feed Apps:** Progressive loading (Pattern 2 - your current)\n   - Fast initial render\n   - Load as user scrolls\n\n3. **Professional Apps:** Hybrid (Pattern 3)\n   - Critical assets upfront\n   - Background pre-fetch\n   - Best UX but more complex\n\n---\n\n## Recommendation for Your App\n\n**Given:**\n- ~150-250 total assets\n- Each image ~1-2MB\n- Carousel-based UI (not infinite scroll)\n- Kids' app (should feel polished)\n\n**Best Approach: Hybrid (Option 3, simplified)**\n\n1. **On Startup:**\n   - Show loading screen with progress bar",

        "contents": "- Consistent audio session setup\n- Standard background music loading\n- Proper cleanup in &#96;deinit&#96;\n- Protocol conformance (&#96;GameAudioServiceProtocol&#96;)\n\n**Subclasses must override:**\n- &#96;assetBaseURL: String&#96; - Base URL for game assets\n- &#96;musicFilename: String&#96; - Name of the music file\n\n### MainView Integration\n\n**Location:** &#96;Views/MainView.swift&#96;\n\nFor each minigame, add:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\n.fullScreenCover(isPresented: $showGameName) {\n    GameNameView(...)\n}\n.onChange(of: showGameName) { oldValue, newValue in\n    // Coordinate music with game lifecycle\n    MusicService.shared.setGameActive(newValue)\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Current Games:**\n- ✅ WaypointGame - Integrated\n- ⏳ GoonPopper - Ready for integration\n- ⏳ MemoryGame - Ready for integration\n- ⏳ Future games - Follow same pattern\n\n## Benefits\n\n✅ **Decoupled Services** - Each service manages its own audio independently  \n✅ **Simple Coordination** - Just pause/resume based on game state  \n✅ **No Central Manager** - Services remain independent  \n✅ **Consistent Pattern** - All games follow the same approach  \n✅ **Automatic Cleanup** - Game audio stops when views are dismissed  \n✅ **State Preservation** - Main music remembers if it was playing\n\n## Audio Session Management\n\n### Category: &#96;.playback&#96;\n- Allows background audio\n- Required for music playback\n\n### Options: &#96;.mixWithOthers&#96;\n- Game audio services use this option\n- Allows game audio to mix with system sounds\n- Prevents conflicts with other audio sources\n\n### Session Activation\n- Each service calls &#96;setActive(true)&#96; independently\n- iOS handles session management automatically\n- No conflicts because services coordinate via lifecycle\n\n## Adding a New Minigame with Audio\n\n### Step 1: Create Audio Service\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;swift\nclass NewGameAudioService: BaseGameAudioService {\n    override var assetBaseURL: String {\n        ",
